raw_result.summary: Resolved plan-review-03 findings by requiring a minimal executable generator, fixing the callable Web authorization boundary, and aligning plan currentness with the corrected specification; repeat independent review remains required.

finding_resolutions.P-18.4-02: The plan now requires one minimal Vulgata.OctoberGenerator executable in this story. Its prepare/select startup modes call the same shared Core setup policy and Infrastructure selector as conditional October Web; actual two-host PostgreSQL selection and mismatch refusal are testable without implementing generation, Worker dispatch, JDT-LS, CodeGraph or Knowledge.
finding_resolutions.P-18.4-03: The Constitution Check now acknowledges required APIs. The shared contract fixes four plural-resource POST routes, closed typed request/result fields, cookie/antiforgery operator proof, separate target-scoped mutual-TLS generator proof, current-authority mapping, cancellation/deadline and sanitized 400/401/403/503 ProblemDetails. The Story 18.1 verifier type and closed Worker functions remain unchanged.
finding_resolutions.P-18.4-04: The plan now states that the current specification already reflects integrated Story 18.1; only repeat plan validation/review remains. It does not claim the Story 18.4 production approval adapter is qualified.

raw_result.feasibility: No generator executable exists in the integrated source, so the new minimal .NET host is an in-scope deliverable for Story 18.4 acceptance. The existing Web Identity/Data Protection and API pipeline support the ordinary operator side; the plan now makes generator client-certificate validation and target allowlisting explicit rather than assuming the operator grant authenticates the process. Certificate and owned database provisioning are qualification prerequisites, not assumed resources.
raw_result.invariants: A Web-issued selection digest binds the full typed setup selection; Web recomputes it for generator validation and the shared policy compares it before writes. Generator and Web call one selector, never a latest-batch query. A source approval remains exact, live, revocable and separate from startup authorization; only Story 18.1's issuer grants a context. Internal API denial/unavailability cannot become cached allow or source-tool readiness.
raw_result.migration_and_compatibility: The new executable composes Core/Infrastructure without changing ordinary Web startup. October migration runs only in explicitly authorized prepare mode; select is read-only over setup metadata. Dedicated October schema/history/model and two owned PostgreSQL target tests remain required. Ordinary Identity/domain EF model, migrations and routes stay at their existing boundary.
raw_result.constitution_and_architecture: The revised API obeys Constitution III's plural-resource, validation, ProblemDetails and API 401/403 requirements and V's protected authority; Core/Infrastructure/Web/Agent ownership remains aligned with Constitution I and the architecture spine. The separate generator is only a setup/selection shell for O-FR17/O-FR18, not a Scan or Knowledge implementation.
raw_result.test_seams_and_lessons: Public-seam tests can call all four routes with controlled operator identity and owned generator certificates, then exercise the actual generator executable and conditional Web against two runner-owned PostgreSQL databases. This addresses the callable-seam lesson; tests/helpers require suites.json classification and the configured eng/test.ps1 runner. Hash-bound plan files retain canonical LF. No behavioral RED/GREEN or runtime result is claimed by this document correction.
raw_result.implementation_design_shape: One front-matter block retains architecture classification. Existing IDs remain valid; new ID-I06, ID-X04 and ID-C04 use exact required headings and syntax. The installed deterministic content validator returned no errors; git diff --check passed. The root owns path/hash-bound workflow validation after mapping.

They do not add, expose or materially change the accepted Story 18.1 Worker Agent functions, a Scan strategy, or a current PRD requirement, so no AGENTS.md planned-change trigger is established on this scope. The root must judge the accepted verdict and any separate architecture-authority conflict before tasks; this self-review is not approval.
